characters.name: Jesse Vane
characters.goal: determine the cause of the manifold rupture

bag.occupation: yard safety inspector and chief fitter

characters.name: Orson Dunlow
characters.goal: contain scandal before morning acquisition audit

characters.name: Donald Pell
characters.goal: assign official blame for the death

bag.environment: damp subterranean brick cellar beneath the high-pressure steam boilers
elevated pine-paneled office overlooking the yard track sidings
corrugated zinc hut beside the water tower containing tools and gear pegs
long brick workshop filled with belt-driven lathes and swarf bins
timber guard booth with barrier gate and official turnstile

premise.logline: A mystery in a working town, where the person who has to find out what happened is also the person who will be blamed for it.

plot_shape.name: Mystery
plot_shape.central_question: What actually happened, and who is willing to say so?

phases.name: Disturbance
phases.purpose: A wrong surfaces and someone is obliged to look into it.

phases.name: Inquiry
phases.purpose: Evidence accumulates, most of it true and misread.

phases.name: Wrong turn
phases.purpose: A reading of the evidence that is coherent and wrong collapses.

phases.name: Solution
phases.purpose: The true account, assembled only from what the reader has already been shown.

phases.name: Cost
phases.purpose: What knowing costs the person who found out.

cast_roles.purpose: Carries the reader through the inquiry and pays its cost.
Has a reason to keep the true account from being assembled.
Holds one true piece and misunderstands its meaning.
The reason the question matters at all.

obligatory_moves: Every element of the true account is on the page before it is stated.
At least one true detail is shown early in a context that makes it look irrelevant.
The wrong reading is defensible on the evidence available when it is made.

events.summary: Jesse examines Toby Callow's body beside the ruptured steam manifold as Constable Pell threatens Jesse with sole criminal liability.
events.dramatic_function: Establishes the disturbance, the central stakes, and the immediate personal peril hanging over the investigator.
beats: Jesse discovers Toby's body pinned under the sheared steam header pipe in the flooded crawlspace.
Constable Pell warns Jesse that under the town works compact, Jesse's inspection signature makes him legally liable for manslaughter.
Superintendent Dunlow demands Jesse inspect the rupture immediately and clear the works before the morning railway audit.

state_changes.value: prove the rupture was caused by tampering rather than inspection negligence

events.summary: Dunlow reviews the plant ledger with Jesse in the yard office, snapping an indelible purple copying pencil while ordering the inquiry shut down.
events.dramatic_function: Plants the unique indelible pencil casually during an administrative confrontation about the upcoming audit.
beats: Jesse asks for the key vault register to see who had night access to the high-pressure valves.
Dunlow marks the morning audit timetable with an imported purple aniline pencil, snapping the lead and dusting his desk blotter.
Dunlow threatens to fire Jesse on the spot if he raises rumors of mechanical failure instead of apprentice error.

events.summary: Jesse retrieves his test gauges from the maintenance shack and notices torn yellow threads caught on the cuff of his spare work coat.
events.dramatic_function: Plants the frayed coat thread detail while Jesse gathers his mechanical inspection tools.
beats: Jesse unlocks his equipment cabinet to take down his calibrated brass pressure gauges.
He sees his spare yellow-waxed mackinaw hanging crooked on the peg with frayed threads snagged on the door hasp.
Jesse grumbles about careless yard hands borrowing gear without asking, grabs his flashlight, and heads back out.

events.summary: Martha Callow confronts Jesse at the gatehouse railing, accusing him of sending Toby into a condemned line to protect his own safety record.
events.dramatic_function: Elevates the community antagonism and anchors the emotional imperative of the wronged party.
beats: Martha demands that Jesse look her in the face and explain why her boy was ordered into the cellar at midnight.
Jesse vows to Martha that he will establish whether the boiler was tampered with before Constable Pell closes the case.
Clara Fenn warns Jesse quietly that Pell is already writing up an affidavit based on what people saw in the fog.

events.summary: Clara admits to Jesse that she logged a figure wearing his yellow waxed mackinaw crossing toward the boiler house at two in the morning.
events.dramatic_function: Delivers the witness's true but misunderstood piece of evidence that directly implicates the investigator.
beats: Jesse inspects Clara's register to see who passed through the turnstile between midnight and the explosion.
Clara confesses she told Constable Pell she saw Jesse's distinctive yellow coat heading down into the sub-vault at 2:30 AM.
Clara urges Jesse to tell the truth if he went down there to patch a leak without logging the downtime.

events.summary: Jesse searches the machine shop and finds freshly turned nickel-alloy flange bolts hidden under Harlan Kemp's lathe bench.
events.dramatic_function: Plants the mismatched flange bolts in the fitting shop, providing the material base for the wrong turn.
beats: Jesse examines the shop work orders to identify which machinist fabricated fittings for the boiler lines this week.
He uncovers an uncataloged box of high-tensile nickel-alloy flange bolts tucked beneath Harlan's lathe.
Harlan aggressively orders Jesse away from his bench, claiming the bolts are standard scrap turnings.

events.summary: Constable Pell corners Jesse in the fitting shop, brandishing Clara's signed statement and setting a dawn deadline for Jesse's arrest.
events.dramatic_function: Ratchets legal time pressure on Jesse, making the town's impending scapegoating explicit.
beats: Pell informs Jesse that Clara's identification of the yellow mackinaw gives the magistrate sufficient grounds for a warrant.
Jesse insists someone took his spare coat from the unlocked shack to frame him or mask their own identity.
Pell gives Jesse two hours to produce physical proof of an intruder before he is taken into custody for manslaughter.

state_changes.value: secure Jesse's confession before the audit train arrives

events.summary: Jesse reviews Toby's personal effects with Martha in the foreman's shack, noting thick waxy animal tallow coating the boy's work gloves.
events.dramatic_function: Plants the animal tallow residue while showing Martha's suspicion of Jesse's motives.
beats: Jesse inventories Toby's tool pouch to return the personal kit to Martha.
He notices that the boy's heavy leather gauntlets are saturated with stiff animal tallow rather than machine mineral oil.
Martha accuses Jesse of staring at grease to dodge the fact that he sent Toby into a condemned vault.

events.summary: Jesse crawls beneath the fractured manifold header with a lantern, mapping the shear lines and discovering that pressure spiked from behind the wall.
events.dramatic_function: Deepens the physical investigation of the fracture site and confirms deliberate over-pressurization.
beats: Jesse traces the tear along the bronze header and observes sheared flange studs along the rear manifold wall.
He calculates that the pressure surge originated not from the boilers, but from an auxiliary branch feeding into the main stack.
He finds a cracked inspection valve that had been forcibly jammed open with a pipe lever.

events.summary: Jesse returns to the office to report the pressure spike and catches Dunlow hastily pocketing an unauthorized scrap metal manifest.
events.dramatic_function: Misdirects Jesse toward the machinist scrap ring by revealing Dunlow's panic over unauthorized metal inventory.
beats: Jesse reports that the manifold blew because auxiliary steam was forced through an unrated flange.
Dunlow shoves a brass scrap shipping receipt under his blotter and declares that the union machinists have been running pirate castings.
Dunlow tells Jesse to search Harlan's tooling bench before Pell arrests the wrong man.

events.summary: Jesse uses his calipers to match Harlan's nickel-alloy bolts against the manifold's sheared studs, convincing himself he has solved the sabotage.
events.dramatic_function: Assembles the false reading of the evidence, cementing Jesse's plausible but mistaken deduction.
beats: Jesse measures the thread pitch of the nickel bolts from Harlan's bench against the fractured studs from the boiler room.
The thread count matches perfectly, leading Jesse to believe Harlan replaced the factory safety studs with brittle bootleg turnings.
Confident he can clear himself of manslaughter, Jesse gathers the bolts to confront Harlan publicly.

events.summary: Jesse confronts Harlan in the boiler house before Constable Pell, accusing him of causing Toby's death with counterfeit nickel-alloy studs.
events.dramatic_function: The Wrong Turn detonates: the investigator presents an internally consistent case that targets the wrong suspect.
beats: Jesse presents the nickel bolts, accusing Harlan of stealing brass and installing defective home-turned studs on the manifold.
Constable Pell grabs Harlan by the coat, declaring the manslaughter case resolved before the audit train arrives.
Harlan screams that he never touched Boiler Three and that Jesse is fabricating evidence to save his own neck.

events.summary: At the gatehouse, Clara pulls the town lockup slip showing Harlan was jailed for public drunkenness until four in the morning, destroying Jesse's case.
events.dramatic_function: The false hypothesis completely collapses under indisputable third-party documentation.
beats: Clara produces the town lockup receipt stamped by the desk sergeant, proving Harlan was behind bars from midnight to 4:00 AM.
Pell releases Harlan immediately and turns on Jesse in outrage for concocting a reckless frame-up.
Jesse realizes with mounting dread that the matching bolt thread was purely circumstantial and that his time has run out.

events.summary: Pell marches Jesse into the foreman's shack beside Martha, giving him thirty minutes before formal arrest while Martha curses his cowardice.
events.dramatic_function: The investigator hits rock bottom, utterly discredited, facing imminent ruin and total community contempt.
beats: Martha denounces Jesse for trying to pin her boy's slaughter on an innocent lathe operator.
Pell lays out the arrest warrant on the workbench and announces the rail company van will transport Jesse to the county seat at dawn.
Pell leaves Jesse under shack guard while he goes to the gate to meet the incoming auditor.

events.summary: Left alone with Martha, Jesse melts the grease from Toby's gloves over a spirit lamp and recognizes tallow used solely in the old unmetered bypass.
events.dramatic_function: The pivotal realization: re-evaluating the physical residue unlocks the true mechanical crime.
beats: Jesse heats the grease scrapings from Toby's gloves over his burner, smelling scorched animal fat and resin packing.
He realizes that tallow was never used in modern boilers; it was only packed into the condemned 1880 bypass that skirts the city steam meter.
Jesse deduces that Toby was ordered to open an illegal bypass line to fake steam capacity for the audit.

state_changes.value: expose the illegal bypass and its true operator

events.summary: Jesse slips into the bypass tunnel, finding torn yellow coat threads on the valve wheel and proving it was forced clockwise by a right-handed man.
events.dramatic_function: Connects the physical proof at the scene directly to the stolen coat and eliminates Toby as the valve operator.
beats: Jesse pulls away the bricking behind the boiler and exposes the unauthorized bypass pipe packed with fresh tallow.
He retrieves frayed yellow waxed-canvas threads wedged tight inside the petcock wheel spokes, matching his shack coat.
He observes that the bypass cheater bar was pulled right-handed with massive force, impossible for Toby who worked left-handed due to missing right fingers.

events.summary: Jesse corners Dunlow in his office, matching the purple aniline ink on the forged bypass work slip to Dunlow's German copying pencil.
events.dramatic_function: The solution is stated: the investigator assembles the complete true account and traps the concealer.
beats: Jesse lays the bypass valve tag on Dunlow's desk beside the broken yellow threads and the animal tallow residue.
He shows that the forged initials authorizing the pressure diversion were written in Dunlow's distinct purple aniline indelible pencil.
Jesse exposes how Dunlow wore Jesse's spare coat into the sub-vault, forced the bypass to trick the audit, and fled when the tallow seal gave way.

events.summary: Jesse drags Dunlow to the yard gate before Pell and Martha, forcing Dunlow to show his scalded wrist and confess to the illegal bypass.
events.dramatic_function: Public resolution of the mystery; the scapegoat forces the true account onto the record in front of all parties.
beats: Jesse strips back Dunlow's cuff, exposing fresh superheated steam burns on his right forearm where the bypass flared.
Faced with the purple pencil slip, the threads, and his burns, Dunlow breaks down and admits he caused the blowout to pass the audit.
Constable Pell drops the warrant against Jesse and locks the cuffs onto Superintendent Dunlow.

events.summary: The visiting railway auditor condemns the plant due to the illegal bypass, padlocking the yard gate and leaving the town destitute.
events.dramatic_function: First beat of the cost: proving the truth triggers immediate systemic collapse and community ruin.
beats: The railway auditor cancels the acquisition contract and padlocks the main gatehouse on grounds of structural fraud.
Harlan and the arriving day-shift workers realize the works are shuttered forever and turn their bitter rage on Jesse for speaking up.
Martha tells Jesse that while he cleared Toby's name, he has starved every living child in Dunlow.

state_changes.value: accept the personal cost of the truth

events.summary: Jesse packs his gauges in the abandoned maintenance shack, exiled by the community he saved from a lie, and walks down the tracks alone.
events.dramatic_function: The final cost paid: thematic completion of the investigator's isolation in a working town that cannot forgive what he proved.
beats: Jesse wraps his brass calipers in oiled cloth and takes his nameplate off the maintenance cabinet.
He looks out at the cold chimneys of the shuttered works, knowing he is officially blameless but completely unemployable.
Jesse hoists his tool bag onto his shoulder and steps onto the railway ties, heading out of the valley into the grey dawn.
